title: Sort your Downloads folder with a local agent you approve
summary: A developer built SlothDesk, where a local Qwen model proposes a category for each Downloads file and nothing moves until the user approves, with one-click undo.
agent_role: The agent inspects file details with three read-only tools and proposes a category and destination for each file. The human reviews and approves the plan; ordinary code performs the moves.
outcome: Author reports a working dashboard with 28 automatic tests; no usage numbers given.
what_they_did: Anirudha Basu Thakur built SlothDesk with help from Google Antigravity. A small model running on a laptop looks at each file in Downloads and suggests a folder like Documents or Archives. The user approves the whole plan before anything moves.
how_it_went: The author shows a working app that never overwrites files, re-checks each file before moving it, and keeps a log for one-click undo.
worth_knowing: A commenter asked whether files changed after the scan are skipped silently, warning that silent skips can make users think the tool is broken.
prompt: Look through my [Downloads folder path] and propose a folder for each loose file: Documents, Images, Videos, Audio, Archives, Code or Other. Show me a table with each file, the suggested folder and a short reason. Don't move, rename or delete anything until I approve. Never overwrite an existing file, and keep a list of moves so I can undo them.

curation.rationale: A working local agent that proposes file moves with read-only tools and waits for approval, with code and tests; useful everyday task but no real-world results reported.
